name: Security header added without 'always' (dropped on error responses)
attack_scenario: An attacker triggers an error or redirect response that lacks HSTS/CSP/X-Frame-Options, then uses SSL-stripping or clickjacking on that unprotected response path the developer believed was covered.
negative_test_hint: request a missing page such as "/no-such-page" and assert the 404 response still includes Strict-Transport-Security and the other security headers

exemplar.explanation: Without the 'always' flag nginx applies add_header only to 2xx/3xx-family responses, so security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options) are silently dropped on 4xx/5xx pages. An attacker can abuse those unprotected error or redirect responses for SSL-stripping or clickjacking; adding 'always' emits the headers on every response.
